title: What Happened to Hitler's Sister After the War
topic: What Happened to Hitler's Sister After the War

beats.narration: In June 1946, American intelligence agents operated high in the Bavarian Alps.
Just miles away lay the ruined alpine retreat of Adolf Hitler at the Berghof.

beats.narration: Allied units were methodically gathering remnants of the fallen Third Reich.

beats.narration: In a secluded mountain inn near Berchtesgaden, they detained an unassuming woman.
beats.search_query: American soldiers at Berchtesgaden toast victory 1945

beats.narration: She had arrived as a refugee, possessing only a single worn suitcase.
beats.search_query: Displaced Persons and Refugees in Germany 1945 suitcase

beats.narration: Her refugee documents bore the false name of Paula Wolff.
Living in complete isolation, she survived on a meager six marks a day.
To the authorities, she appeared as merely another destitute civilian.
When military investigators opened the classified interrogation dossier,

beats.narration: the records confirmed her lineage to the family grave in Leonding.
beats.search_query: Leonding grave of Hitler parents Austria

beats.narration: She was the youngest daughter of Alois and Klara Hitler.
beats.search_query: Klara Hitler mother of Adolf Hitler portrait

beats.narration: And the only surviving full sister of Adolf Hitler.
During intensive questioning, she described a distant brother who had severed personal contact.
Living apart, she claimed total ignorance of his inner circle.
When questioned about the concentration camps, she remained in denial.
beats.search_query: Hitler speech in the Reichstag historical

beats.narration: I cannot believe, she insisted, that my brother ordered such crimes.
Yet declassified wartime files revealed a darker connection.
Paula had been secretly engaged to Doctor Erwin Jekelius at Vienna Steinhof clinic.
Jekelius was a leading architect of the Aktion T4 extermination program.
beats.search_query: Steinhof memorial stone NS victims Vienna

beats.narration: Under his direction, thousands of psychiatric patients were systematically murdered.
Over thirty-two hundred innocent victims were dispatched to Hartheim Castle.
Inside the secluded castle walls, industrial gas chambers operated in absolute secrecy.
Among those executed was Aloisia Veit, a cousin of the Hitler family.
The machinery of death consumed even relatives of the dictator himself.
Following months in custody, Paula was cleared of active war crimes.
beats.search_query: Hitler and Eva Braun wedding documents 1945

beats.narration: She petitioned the courts for her legal share of her brother residual estate.
beats.search_query: Adolf Hitler and Martin Bormann Berghof

beats.narration: The Bavarian state confiscated all properties and publishing rights.
Penniless, she survived on welfare and the charity of local acquaintances.
In 1959, she broke years of silence to give her only television interview.
One year later, on June 1st, 1960, she passed away in Berchtesgaden.
She was buried under the name Paula Wolff in the mountain cemetery.
With her death, the immediate bloodline of Adolf Hitler came to an end.
